card.name: Endings of long adjectives in medical terms
card.fires_on: The closing piece of a long adjective-like word after its stem, such as ischem-ic, Monob-asic, aque-ous, c-yclic and Zeithistor-ische. It appears in label text and in formal names.

modes.label: Chemical or pathway adjectives
modes.description: Final piece of a chemical or biological adjective just before a noun.
modes.example: Consistent with the effects of PDE5 inhibition on the nitric oxide/c<<yclic>> guanosine monophosphate pathway,

modes.label: Condition or drug-name adjectives
modes.description: Ending piece of a condition or salt name that is split into parts.
modes.example: Myocardial infarction or unstable ischem<<ic>> heart disease in the last 6 months

modes.label: Foreign or capitalized adjective
modes.description: Ending of a long adjective in a German institute name or an all-caps warning.
modes.example: THE EXTRAPYRAMID<<AL>> SYMPTOMS WHICH CAN OCC

card.plain: It marks the last piece of a long medical adjective, like the ending of ischemic or aqueous, just before the noun it describes.
